detail.longDescription: I built a benchmark from 32 problems archived from Google's 2015 internal code-golf contest (go/codegolf), replicating the original 2015 runtimes for JS, Python, C++, and Haskell alongside four added languages. Models get 30 minutes per problem/language cell and are scored by byte count against the old human records. Besides the leaderboard and problem pages, two short sections on the site might be worth a look for HN readers: Finding a different approach ( https://bjin.github.io/go-codegolf-benchmark/#why/finding-a-... ) walks through a few unexpected solutions to seemingly straightforward problems. Why I built this ( https://bjin.github.io/go-codegolf-benchmark/#about/why-i-bu... ) is a personal note on the mixed feelings of seeing models beat records that people spent hours on back in 2015. Thanks for taking a look!
